reading.text:
Unit: def:LevyStochCalc.Poisson.Compensated.MarkStep.integral (reading locked before any Lean is seen)

Paper notion. The compensated Poisson integral of the elementary marked integrand (unit 17):
   int_0^t int_E phi(s,e) Ntilde(ds,de) = sum_{k,j} xi_{k,j} * Ntilde((t_k ^ t, t_{k+1} ^ t] x B_j),
with Ntilde(A) = N(A) - (Leb (x) nu)(A) for A of finite intensity (Section 2, line 234).
At t = terminal time (or with no time argument) it is sum xi_{k,j} Ntilde((t_k,t_{k+1}] x B_j).

What a faithful Lean definition must be.
- As above, using the driver's Poisson random measure N and the intensity Leb (x) nu with the paper's
  nu, compensated by SUBTRACTING the intensity of the same set. Real-valued: N(A) in R>=0oo converted to a
  real; when N(A) = oo (a null event for finite-intensity A) the junk value is harmless; when nu(B_j) = oo,
  the formula is meaningless and must not be relied on (the structure or the uses must require finite
  measure).
- The slab endpoints must be the ones of eval (unit 21); left-open/right-closed vs other conventions are
  harmless for N-counts only up to the null event that N charges {t_k} x B_j (probability 0 for fixed t_k).
- If time-indexed, truncation at t (t_k ^ t, t_{k+1} ^ t].

comparison.text:
Comparison: def:LevyStochCalc.Poisson.Compensated.MarkStep.integral
(Poisson/MarkStepIsometry.lean:91-95; PoissonRandomMeasure.compensated, RandomMeasure.lean.)

- Reading: sum_{k,j} xi_{k,j} Ntilde((t_k ^ t, t_{k+1} ^ t] x B_j), Ntilde(A) = N(A) - (Leb (x) nu)(A),
  with the driver's N and the paper's nu; real-valued; junk on the null event N(A) = oo harmless; finite
  measure of B_j required; same slabs as eval; truncation at t.
- Lean: integral N G t omega = sum_{i < N_0} sum_k xi i k omega *
  N.compensated (Ioc (min p_i t) (min p_{i+1} t) x B k) omega, with
  compensated A omega = (N omega A).toReal - (referenceIntensity nu A).toReal and referenceIntensity nu =
  Lebesgue|[0,oo) (x) nu. Since B k has finite nu-measure (field B_finite) and the slab is bounded, the
  intensity is finite (no junk in the second term), and N(A) is a.s. a natural number (integer_valued), so
  toReal is junk only on a null set. Slabs (min p_i t, min p_{i+1} t] match eval's (p_i, p_{i+1}]
  truncated at t; for t <= 0 every slab is empty and the integral is 0 (p_0 = 0, increasing grid).
- N is a parameter (any PRM with intensity nu on the same space): the driver's N is passed at the uses.

Verdict: faithful.
